pamphlet_excerpts: Oxidation Process: Rapid oxidation releases heat and light energy through sustained chemical molecular conversion.
Tetrahedron Components: Self-sustaining combustion demands fuel, oxygen, sufficient heat, and an uninterrupted chain reaction.
Combustion Products: Incomplete burning produces toxic carbon monoxide gas along with airborne particulate smoke.
Thermal Transfer: Convection circulates superheated buoyant gases vertically toward enclosed interior ceiling surfaces.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Fuel Classification: Identify whether the primary combustible matter is solid cellulose, liquid, or gas.
Step 2 - Environment Assessment: Measure ambient oxygen levels and evaluate ventilation pathways feeding incoming airflow.
Step 3 - Thermal Tracking: Locate ignition sources and track conduction paths through connected structural metal framing.
Step 4 - Chain Disruption: Introduce a dry chemical suppression agent to stop gas-phase radical propagation reactions.

left_points: (1a) Combustion and Oxidation Fundamentals: Fire is rapid oxidation that transforms combustible materials into heated gas compounds. Solids and liquids must undergo pyrolysis or vaporization before flaming ignition occurs.

(1b) Fire Tetrahedron and Products: The fire tetrahedron models the four elements necessary to maintain flaming combustion. Removing any single component halts the ongoing chemical process and extinguishes the fire.
right_points: (1c) Fire Development Life Cycle: Fires develop through distinct stages comprising incipient, growth, fully developed, and decay phases. Flashover represents a sudden transition driven by radiant heat feedback from ceiling smoke layers.

(1d) Thermal Energy Transfer Methods: Heat moves via conduction through physical solids, convection across moving fluids and gases, and thermal radiation across open spaces. Convective currents drive hot gases upward while radiation ignites adjacent combustible objects.

pamphlet_excerpts: Suppression Technique: Dropping immediately to the ground eliminates the upward chimney effect on clothing.
Smothering Motion: Rolling back and forth smothers active flames by depriving fabric of air.
Cooling Protocol: Cool clean water stabilizes skin temperature and stops deeper tissue thermal destruction.
Inhalation Hazards: Toxic smoke particles sear delicate bronchial linings and cause severe airway swelling.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Immediate Stop: Stop walking or running instantly to prevent feeding ambient airflow into flames.
Step 2 - Ground Drop: Drop directly to the ground and shield facial skin with both hands.
Step 3 - Lateral Roll: Roll back and forth continuously across ground surfaces until all flames collapse.
Step 4 - Water Cooling: Apply clean cool potable water over burned skin for ten full minutes.

Step 3 - Origin Identification: Uncover the specific physical area where fuel and ignition source first united.
Step 4 - Cause Categorization: Assign origin classification according to physical evidence and laboratory test results.

Match Extinguishment: Hold extinguished matches between bare fingers to confirm the wooden stick is cold.
Drown and Stir: Drown embers in water, stir with a stick, and drown repeatedly until cold.
Fuel Isolation: Store compressed liquid fuel canisters away from direct sunlight and radiant campfire heat.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Site Clearing: Rake duff and pine needles ten feet outward exposing bare damp mineral soil.
Step 2 - Kindling Assembly: Stack dry tinder shavings inside a loose tepee surrounded by finger-sized kindling.
Step 3 - Shielded Ignition: Strike match away from body and ignite tinder base from upwind sheltered position.
Step 4 - Complete Extinguishment: Drown burning embers with water, stir ashes, and feel coals with bare hands.
